figures.label: S13
figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 13. Phase identification of the Li-Ag alloy from the operando XRD patterns. The powder patterns of LLZO, Ag, and the  and 3-phases were obtained from the ICDD database (LLZO: PDF# 01-080-6142, Ag: PDF# 00-004-0783, : PDF# 04-003-6862, 3: PDF# 04-003-2052). The powder patterns of the 2- and -phases were simulated from the structures that retain the same - brass space group as the 3-phase1 with lattice parameters obtained from the experimental XRD patterns. The powder pattern of the Li3Ag was also simulated from the crystal structure taken from the Materials Project database (mp-865875), the lattice parameters of which were refined by fitting the experimental XRD patterns.

figures.label: S22
figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 22. Microstructural changes during TEM sample preparation using the conventional FIB process. FIB-SEM images for (a–c) the slope milling and lift-out process with the deposition of a surface protective layer. Although the surface protective layer of Pt was intended to be deposited with a thickness of approximately 500 nm (according to the experimental protocol developed on a Si substrate), its thickness was more than 2 m, as shown in (b). The thicker Pt layer is attributed to the reaction of Li and Pt. During final thinning after lifting out the sample onto the TEM grid, (d and e) the microstructure of the Li-Ag layer was changed by the Ga+ beam, and (f) dendritic Li grew from the surface protective layer (Pt and C deposition). The TEM sample was transferred from the glove box to FIB without exposure to air using an airtight chamber.

The sample was checked for impurities by an XPS survey scan, and only Cl was detected, which was a residue of the HCl used to wash the surface after surface polishing.
